events.credibility_reason: Thesis never located or read; existence, content and committee approval are inferred from a reference entry seen in a search snippet.

why: The statement asks for a characterisation of word-representable planar graphs. Roy–Hariharasubramanian (May 2026) claims a forbidden-induced-subgraph characterisation for near-triangulations, a proper planar subclass, and the authors themselves say the planar problem is open: case, unreviewed preprint, no AI. Its corrections of Glen and Kitaev–Sun are not by themselves reasons to doubt it; the misstatement of Glen's theorem is noted in doubts. The 2014–2016 papers are journal-published restricted-class characterisations (case, digested, pre-snapshot). Hauser's thesis is a case by title only and was never read, so it is unreviewed and doubtful. 1-11-representability, modular decomposition/lexicographic products and tensor products are different questions (variant). Kitaev–Sun concerns non-planar graphs and a 7-vertex list (none). Hefty et al. 2024 has no planar content that the record established (none, date year-only so null). Melon graphs are series-parallel, so they are 3-colourable and already known to be word-representable; a representation-number bound adds nothing to the characterisation (none). Direction is left null on the case rows because a characterisation of a subclass does not confirm or refute a conjecture.
doubts: The Roy paper's theorems come from a small-model summary of the HTML version, not a verbatim read. It restates Glen's result as 'iff perfect', while Glen's abstract says 'iff 3-colourable', and that is unresolved. The record also says Roy answers the separate Kitaev–Lozin item on near-triangulations containing K4; if that item appears as its own bullet on the frozen list, this event belongs to that bullet as well.
